mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate above 4.5% for two consecutive months signals a restrictive monetary stance, raising discount rates and reducing present value of corporate cash flows, leading to negative S&P 500 20-day returns.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5%) in at least 70% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) of more than 2% coincident with a housing starts drop (HOUST) below 1.8 million signals weakening aggregate demand, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly unemployment rate (UNRATE) below 4.0% for three consecutive months signals a tight labor market, which increases wage pressures and input costs, ultimately reducing corporate margins and leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) of more than 0.5% alongside a concurrent drop in real retail sales (RSAFS) below $340 billion signals weakening manufacturing and consumer demand, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day returns are positive in more than 40% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp one-month decline in the federal funds rate below 3.0% signals an emergency easing, which boosts liquidity and lowers risk premiums, producing positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS drops below 3.0% in one month
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are not significantly positive (> +0.5%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A concurrent rise in both unemployment rate (UNRATE) and payrolls (PAYEMS) month-over-month above 0.4% indicates a paradoxical labor market shock (e.g., mass layoffs with temporary rehiring), which increases uncertainty and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE change > 0.4% AND PAYEMS change > 40000 in the same month
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5%) in at least 50% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent annual increase in the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) above 4.0% for six consecutive months signals entrenched inflation, prompting anticipatory monetary tightening and higher discount rates, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous monthly decline in both industrial production (INDPRO) and housing starts (HOUST) of more than 0.4% and below 1800 respectively signals a broad-based contraction in manufacturing and construction, which reduces earnings visibility and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5%) in at least 50% of triggered episodes.
